Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

amorem 1.2.0

Bug fixes

  • rem(method = "gam") warns when rows with missing covariate values are left out of the fit, and records which rows it used (fit$rows, with fit$n counting only those). gof_rem() keeps the same rows when given the full data; it stopped with “non-conformable arguments” before.

  • sample_non_events(scope = "citation") always draws the citing paper and the cited papers from separate pools. Under the mode = "one" default of 1.1.0 it pooled them, so most controls had a sender other than the citing paper.

  • rem(method = "nn") and nn_uncertainty() no longer change the caller’s random-number state when given a seed (CRAN policy); fitted results are unchanged.

  • Partial-dependence curves of plot() on neural fits and of nn_uncertainty() span the 1st to 99th percentile of each feature instead of the mean ± 2 standard deviations, which reached below the data for skewed, non-negative statistics.

  • Concordance of neural fits splits a tied top score evenly between the tied candidates; it gave the whole stratum to the event.

  • simulate_relational_events(method = "tau_leap") stops with a message when a single step would draw more than ten million events, which happens when an effect grows without bound; it could exhaust memory.

New features

  • gof_rem() tests a model fitted with rem(method = "gam") with cumulative martingale residuals (Boschi & Wit 2025): over event time (test = "time"), over the quantiles of a covariate (test = "functional_form", which detects a wrong shape of the effect), or over the quantiles weighted by the term’s basis (test = "functional_form_score"). It works on linear and smooth terms of the fitted model, and its null distribution is a multiplier bootstrap that subtracts the drift from estimating the coefficients. It has print() and plot() methods (plot() takes main and a legend position). The existing gof_univariate(), gof_multivariate(), gof_global() and gof_auxiliary() are unchanged.

  • rem() fits store the name of their time column.

Datasets

  • New alien_mammals: the risk table of the first records of alien mammals with the covariates of Juozaitienė et al. (2023) (distance to the nearest invaded region, trade, temperature difference, colonial ties, land use), and the never-at-risk pairs and species entry years as attributes; used in the species-invasion section of the software paper.

  • New event logs, all under licences that allow redistribution: copenhagen_calls, copenhagen_sms and copenhagen_actors (Copenhagen Networks Study, MIT); us_leader_visits (leader-to-leader visits to and from the United States, 1945-2019, CC0); football_results (men’s international football matches since 1872, CC0); ucdp_dyads (UCDP armed-conflict dyads, 1946-2025, CC BY 4.0); alien_invasions (first records of alien species by region, 1880-2005, CC0).

  • New hyperevent log: congress_bills_118, one sponsor and the cosponsors of each bill of the 118th US Congress, with congress_members_118 (public domain).

  • New global covariates: oni (Oceanic Nino Index since 1950), daily_weather (NOAA daily temperature and precipitation for the cities of the bundled email and messaging logs) and public_holidays.

  • radoslaw_email is rebuilt from the authors’ CC0 release (Nurek & Michalski 2020, doi:10.7910/DVN/6Z3CGX). It keeps the original employee ids, which match the new radoslaw_hierarchy (who reports to whom), and its timestamps are read as Warsaw local time. The previous copy, from Network Repository, read them as UTC, so it ignored daylight saving time: events sent during Polish summer time are now one hour earlier relative to the first event, and unix_origin is one hour earlier. The number of events and each employee’s activity are unchanged.

  • The pkgdown site has a data catalogue: licences, download code and structural profiles of 78 relational-event datasets and covariates, including the many whose licences do not allow amorem to redistribute them.

amorem 1.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-10-17

Bug fixes

  • Endogenous statistics on case-control data no longer count the sampled controls as events. endogenous_features() on the output of sample_non_events() (a 0/1 event column with control rows) now builds the network history from the event == 1 rows only; the controls read it but never enter it. Before, every row updated the history, so each statistic also counted hypothetical dyads. This was the default path inside compare_models(), compare_models_smooth(), gof(), martingale_residuals() and the vignettes. On six simulated datasets with a reciprocity effect of 0.3, the estimate moved from 0.20 to 0.31 on average. Results of those functions change and should be re-run. Pass history_log = event_log to treat every row as an event.

  • rem() evaluates tv() and tvnl() terms at each row’s own time. When data has time_ev / time_nv instead of a single time column (the wide form of sample_non_events(shift = "exponential")), tv(x) contributes beta(t) x_ev - beta(t*) x_nv and tvnl() uses both times. Before, the event time was used for both rows. Models with a single time column give the same formula and fit as before.

  • compare_models_global() now uses the paper’s time-shifted design. It drew one shift per control row, never shifted the event, never checked the observation window (control times could precede the data), evaluated the controls’ dyadic statistics at the event time, and let sampled controls enter the network history. On simulated data with a global effect of 1 it returned estimates of -1.74, 2.63 and -2.12 over three datasets. It now draws its sample with sample_non_events(shift = "exponential"), computes dyadic statistics against the real history at each row’s own time, evaluates tv / tvnl terms at each row’s own time, and drops events with no control; the same three datasets give 0.85, 1.02 and 1.01. The shift mean is now shift_scale times the average event time (it was times the average inter-arrival time), and a window argument is passed through. Results of earlier compare_models_global() fits change and should be re-run.

  • widen_case_control() and the clogit / nn backends of rem() use the stratum column written by sample_non_events() when stratum = NULL, instead of rebuilding strata as cumsum(case == 1). The rebuilt strata assumed each case was followed by its controls, which stops holding once endogenous_features() re-sorts rows by time with ties, or with shifted controls, and then paired cases with the wrong controls. Data without a stratum column (eventnet output) is handled as before.

  • sample_non_events() risk-set edge cases (#102).

    • exclude_pairs and, under risk = "remove", same-time events are now part of the check for whether any valid control exists, so a stratum whose every alternative is excluded gets no controls instead of stopping with “Unable to sample a valid non-event after max_attempts attempts”.
    • scope = "appearance" no longer falls back to all actors when no actor has appeared yet: the first event gets no controls, and controls are only ever drawn from actors seen in prior events, as documented. Results change for the first stratum(s) of scope = "appearance" fits.
    • Factor sender / receiver columns are coerced to character, so the output columns are character whatever the input type.
    • The documentation of mode states which risk set each mode gives: "two" never draws a receiver-only actor as a control sender (or vice versa), so networks with one node set should use mode = "one".
    • The unreachable empty-pool fallbacks in the pair sampler were removed.

Changes in behaviour

  • sample_non_events() now defaults to mode = "one", the risk set of networks whose senders and receivers are one node set, and the default of compare_models(), compare_models_smooth(), compare_models_global(), gof() and martingale_residuals(). Calls that relied on the old default mode = "two" (bipartite networks) must now pass it.

New features

  • New dataset enso_nino34: the tree-ring reconstruction of the November–January Niño3.4 sea-surface temperature anomaly by Li et al. (2013), one value per year from 1301 to 2005 (NOAA NCEI study 14632), as a global covariate on a yearly clock. The raw NOAA file ships in inst/extdata/enso_nino34/, and data-raw/enso_nino34.R rebuilds the object.

  • vignette("species-invasion") now simulates five centuries of invasions (1500–2005) driven by distance, a neighbour pressure and ENSO. It shows that ordinary case-control sampling gives an ENSO difference of zero in every stratum, and recovers all three effects with time-shifted sampling and rem(), reporting standard errors.

  • Time-shifted case-control sampling for global covariates (#101). sample_non_events(shift = "exponential") implements Section 4 of Lembo, Juozaitienė, Vinciotti & Wit (2025, JRSS-C): one exponential shift per dyad, each control drawn uniformly from the dyads whose back-shifted time lies in the observation window and stored at that time, so covariates that depend only on time no longer cancel within strata. shift_scale sets the mean shift as a multiple of the average event time, as in the paper. Risk-set rules (exclude_pairs, risk = "remove", scope = "appearance") are evaluated at the control’s own time; events with no other dyad in their shifted risk set get no control and are listed in attr(, "shift")$uninformative. The attribute also holds the shift mean, the window and the per-dyad shifts.

  • endogenous_features(history_log = ) and prior_log now work for every statistic, including reciprocity_exp_decay, reciprocity_time_recent and reciprocity_time_first, which the compiled engine does not cover.

  • Per-term basis settings in rem() formulas (#91). Smooth terms take the basis arguments of mgcv::s() / mgcv::te() after the covariate, so terms in one model can use different basis dimensions and types: tv(x, k = 20, bs = "cr") + nl(y, k = 5, bs = "ps"). tvnl() takes one value per margin (tvnl(x, k = c(5, 8))). A new global bs argument joins the global k as the default for terms that set neither; existing formulas give the same model as before.

  • sample_non_events(exclude_concurrent = ) controls whether dyads with an event at the focal event’s own time can be controls. The default keeps the existing behaviour: excluded under risk = "remove", at risk under risk = "standard" (the Breslow convention).

amorem 1.0.1

Bug fixes

  • compare_models() did not stratify on the matched sets under survival before 3.7-3. The Cox formula was built with a namespace-qualified survival::strata(stratum), and terms(specials = ) does not match a qualified call, so the matched-set identifier was silently fitted as an ordinary factor covariate in an unstratified model. Coefficients and the delta_AIC column were unaffected; the absolute log_lik was shifted by -n_events * log(n_strata) and the degrees of freedom inflated by n_strata - 1, so reported AIC values were wrong. The same applied to the frailty() terms on the random-effects path, which is why the coxme two-axis fit did not complete. All four call sites now use bare specials, which every survival version matches, and regression tests assert that AIC == -2 * log_lik + 2 * df and that no stratum dummies enter as covariates. Anyone who published absolute log-likelihood or AIC values from compare_models(n_controls > 1) should re-run them.

amorem 1.0.0

CRAN release: 2026-06-29

First CRAN release, under the name amorem. The package was renamed from the working name amore, which collided (case-insensitively) with the archived CRAN package AMORE. This release consolidates the 0.9.0 development line into the first stable, installable version: the unified rem() front-end (the clogit, gam, and nn backends, including the additive-spline architecture), the Gillespie / tau-leap simulation engine, the endogenous-statistics catalogue, and the martingale-residual goodness-of-fit family. Relative to 0.9.0 the package was renamed to amorem and the exported feature functions dropped their compute_ prefix — compute_endogenous_features() and compute_hyperedge_features() became endogenous_features() and hyperedge_features(); the rest of the API is unchanged.

New features

  • torch training engine for rem(method = "nn"). nn_control(engine = "torch") trains the same model and conditional-logistic loss as the built-in pure-R engine using torch (libtorch autograd + Adam), markedly faster and, with batch_strata, scaling to large event logs (optionally on GPU). The fitted object is interchangeable with the R engine. torch is a Suggests dependency; the torch engine requires equal-sized strata.
  • nn_uncertainty() quantifies uncertainty for a neural fit by a stratum bootstrap, returning partial-dependence uncertainty bands and a concordance confidence interval (with print() and plot() methods) — the inferential counterpart the point-prediction nn backend otherwise lacks.

amorem 0.9.0

New neural backend and a small number of API refinements; the version intended for the first CRAN release.

  • STREAM-style additive splines: nn_control(architecture = "additive_spline", batch_strata = ) fits per-covariate B-spline effects by (mini-batch) stochastic gradient on the exact case-control partial likelihood — the construction of Filippi-Mazzola & Wit (2024, JRSS-C, doi:10.1093/jrsssc/qlae023) — giving interpretable additive smooth curves on the same objective as clogit, with mini-batching for large event logs.
  • New rem(method = "nn") backend: a multilayer perceptron scores every candidate in a case-control stratum and is trained on the conditional-logistic partial likelihood (softmax over each risk set) — a nonlinear, prediction-oriented counterpart of clogit. Pure-R implementation (no extra dependencies), configured via nn_control(); summary() reports in-sample (and, with a validation split, held-out) concordance and plot(type = "pdp") shows per-feature partial-dependence curves.
  • API: the degenerate-logistic backend is now method = "gam" (was "degenerate"); the smooth-term wrappers are tv() / nl() / tvnl() (was tve() / nle() / tvnle()); re() is unchanged.
  • rem()’s case argument now defaults to NULL and is taken from the formula’s left-hand side (e.g. event ~ x) for the clogit/nn backends.
  • widen_case_control() auto-detects the 0/1 indicator column (event or IS_OBSERVED) when case is not given.
  • widen_case_control() now carries the sender/receiver identifiers of the case and its matched control into the output (sender_ev/receiver_ev/ sender_nv/receiver_nv); the new keep_ids argument controls this (default TRUE). The dyads behind each pair are no longer lost, and re() grouping terms can reach the actor levels (#92).
  • rem(method = "gam") now detects long-format case-control input (a event/IS_OBSERVED indicator with control rows) and widens it with widen_case_control() before fitting, emitting a message — instead of silently misreading raw per-row values as event-minus-control differences (#93).
  • compute_endogenous_features() gains a prior_log argument for warm-starting the network state from events that precede the study window: its rows update the running state but never appear in the output, separating warm-starting from the non-event masking role of history_log (#94).
  • cpp_supported_stats() is now exported.

amorem 0.1.0

First release.

  • rem() unified fitter for preprocessed case-control data, with a gam (case-1-control logistic via mgcv::gam()) and a clogit backend.
  • Smooth-term formula wrappers for the gam backend (time-varying, non-linear, time-varying-non-linear) and an re() grouping random effect; re() reproduces the Intro-to-REM tutorial parameterization, and rem() exposes a gam_method argument.
  • Simulation via simulate_relational_events() (Gillespie and tau-leap), the endogenous-statistic feature engine, non-event sampling, and the martingale-residual goodness-of-fit family.
